text: [American Motorists Ins. Co. v. Allied-Sysco Food Services, Inc., supra, 19 CA4th at 1349, 24 CR2d at 110 (disapproved on other grounds by Buss v. Sup.Ct. (Transamerica Ins. Co.) (1997) 16 C4th 35, 65 CR2d 366)] (b) [3:474] Effect of exclusion for claims relating to dismissal: Employment discrimination claims against an employer were covered under a policy that defined “personal injury” to include “discrimination” … notwithstanding an exclusion for “personal injury sustained … as a result of an offense directly or indirectly related to the dismissal of any employee of the Insured.” [Melugin v. Zurich Canada, supra, 50 CA4th at 668, 57 CR2d at 787 (emphasis added)] This “vaguely worded” exclusion did not excuse the insurer's duty to defend claims that the employer had discriminated against its employees during their employment.
